artifacts.name: FCOA Canonical Memory & Intelligence Fabric Node

capability_deltas: FCOA-Ω gains a Windows-native Device-Control Limb for authorized screen, cursor, mouse, keyboard and foreground-window interaction on the owner-controlled PC.
Virtual environments use direct structured adapters first and may fall back to the same desktop input limb when a graphical surface is the only qualified route.
Device control is localhost-only, mission-leased, TTL-bounded, auditable and pause/emergency-stop capable.
Consequential external effects such as messaging, publication, spending, IAM/account changes or destructive provider actions still require a matching mission authority receipt.
The limb does not bypass Windows secure desktop/UAC, fabricate credentials, or override active foreign source fences.

llm_context.external_effect_rule: Consequential effects require separate mission authority receipt; physical input access does not enlarge external authority.
llm_context.hardware_hid_rule: True USB-HID/KVM hardware emulation is a separate optional limb and is not deployed by this update.

route_deltas: Prefer semantic/direct API or browser/VM adapters for virtual environments; use physical desktop input only when it is the best qualified route or direct adapters are absent.
Before any physical input, acquire a short-lived FCOA device lease bound to mission, device, allowed effects and optional foreground-window allowlist.
Read screen/foreground state before effectful input; reject stale, expired, mismatched or unqualified sessions.
All device-control commands append hash-chained audit events and support pause/emergency-stop.
Owner-PC live execution remains unproven while the registered remote device is offline; do not infer physical runtime from source/build proof.
summary: Add FCOA-Ω Device-Control Limb for governed virtual and physical Windows interaction with screen, keyboard and mouse capabilities.
warnings: The current owner PC relay MosianeKK-LPT is offline; live physical input on that device is not yet proven.
This is OS-level Windows input injection, not a physical USB-HID/KVM device.
No secure-desktop/UAC bypass or provider-authority bypass is provided.
